title: Arrival, old Kabul markets, and garden sunset
description: Airport pickup, hotel check-in, and a soft first afternoon focused on Kabul’s historic market streets. The day is paced gently so guests can recover from arrival while still seeing Murad Khane, the bird market, Chicken Street, and Babur’s Gardens if timing allows.

title: Museum, Darulaman, shrines, and Kabul viewpoints
description: A full Kabul touring day connecting national history, restored architecture, religious landmarks, and city viewpoints. The route can be adjusted around traffic, prayer times, and photography sensitivity.

title: Paghman or Qargha morning and departure
description: A short final morning outside the dense city center, usually Qargha Lake or Paghman depending on flight time, followed by airport transfer.

title: Arrival and Kabul old-city orientation
description: Arrival support and an introductory walk through Kabul’s older commercial lanes, useful for guests who want context before moving into surrounding valleys.

title: Core Kabul heritage circuit
description: A focused day on Kabul’s major heritage sites: the National Museum, Darulaman Palace, Babur’s Gardens, and selected religious or viewpoint stops based on access.

title: Panjshir day excursion
description: Early departure north through Parwan toward Panjshir, with valley stops, Massoud Mausoleum, and time along the river corridor before returning to Kabul.

title: Jalalabad corridor or Nangarhar day route
description: A route-dependent eastern day toward Darunta Lake and Jalalabad-area cultural sites when access and timing are suitable. If conditions are weak, the day remains in Kabul.

title: Paghman, Qargha, and west Kabul
description: A relaxed day combining lakeside scenery, Paghman landmarks, and west Kabul neighborhoods. This day also provides flexibility if an earlier day was delayed.

title: Departure support
description: Hotel check-out, final shopping or tea stop if time allows, and airport transfer.

title: Welcome to Kabul, Winter Briefing and Cultural Introduction
description: Airport reception and hotel transfer. A traditional Afghan clothing experience, then the winter road and tour briefing and an inspection of your equipment and cold-weather clothing; the next morning’s Kabul–Bamyan movement is confirmed against weather and road status. Sakhi Shrine follows, with TV Hill if time permits. Food & culture: aush.

title: Journey Through the Winter Highlands to Bamyan
description: Winter road transfer by private 4WD into the central highlands, with timing kept conservative and the road chosen for that week’s conditions. In Bamyan, the Buddha Niches, then Shahr-e-Gholghola if daylight permits. Food & culture: Afghan kabob.

title: Koh-e-Baba Backcountry Skiing Adventure
description: The dedicated backcountry ski day in the Koh-e-Baba Mountains. This is human-powered ski touring, not resort skiing: no lifts and no groomed runs. Route choice depends on snowfall, visibility, wind, avalanche assessment and group ability, and the day is shortened or changed when conditions require it. Winter photography in the high valleys. Food & culture: bolani.

title: Bamyan Heritage and Optional Second Ski Day
description: A flexible day. The heritage plan covers the Buddha Niches, Shahr-e-Gholghola, Shahr-e-Zohak and Dragon Valley. Alternatively, a second ski outing if snow, avalanche and road conditions permit; the second ski day is an option, not a promise. Food & culture: local dried fruits and nuts.

title: Return to Kabul and Traditional Afghan Farewell
description: Bamyan–Kabul winter road transfer, timed conservatively for road and weather. If time permits after arrival: the Mir Zaman box-camera experience, if prearranged, and optional time on Chicken Street. The evening is a traditional Afghan farewell feast. Food & culture: Qabuli palaw.

title: Departure
description: Optional final Chicken Street shopping if your flight time allows, then the airport transfer.

title: Welcome to Kabul
description: Arrival reception and hotel transfer, then Chicken Street, a traditional Afghan clothing and tailoring experience (whether the clothing itself is included in the price is confirmed on your written proposal), and a tour orientation for the valley day ahead. Food & culture: Afghan kabob.

title: Panjshir Valley: Emeralds and History
description: A full day north through Parwan and Jabal Saraj into Panjshir, following the Panjshir River past mountain villages, and back to Kabul the same day; there is no overnight in Panjshir. The Ahmad Shah Massoud Mausoleum, subject to access, and an introduction to the local emerald industry. On privately coordinated tours only, an emerald auction or arranged gemstone trading session is available by special arrangement. Attendance, successful bidding and purchases cannot be promised: they depend on verified auction access, legitimate transactions and seller documentation, and any purchase is subject to customs and export requirements, so export is not automatic. The Paryan Valley extension runs only if time and access allow, and a prearranged auction takes priority if both cannot fit. Food & culture: Afghan green tea.

title: Kabul’s Historic Heritage and Scenic Viewpoints
description: A full Kabul day after the valley: the Kabul National Museum, Darulaman Palace, Sakhi Shrine, and the city views from TV Tower Hill and Wazir Akbar Khan Hill. Food & culture: Qabuli palaw.

title: Farewell to Afghanistan
description: Kahfroshi Bird Market if time permits, then the airport transfer with departure assistance.

title: Welcome to Kabul
description: Airport reception and hotel transfer. Sightseeing is scheduled around your actual flight arrival time, so a late landing means fewer stops today. The journey opens with a traditional Afghan clothing and tailoring experience: choose the cloth and be measured, with the finished clothes collected on Day 6 if arranged (whether the clothing itself is included in the price is confirmed on your written proposal). Then, as time allows, the National Museum of Afghanistan, Darulaman Palace and Babur’s Gardens. Food & culture: traditional Afghan kabob.

title: Journey Through the Highlands to Bamyan
description: A full road day by private 4WD into the central highlands. The road is chosen that week for conditions; on the southern route it climbs through the Wardak Highlands. Arrival is planned for daylight, with a first look at the Buddha Niches cut into the Bamyan cliffs and time in Bamyan Market. Food & culture: Afghan green tea.

title: Discover Ancient Bamyan
description: A day among the valley’s fortress ruins. Shahr-e-Zohak, the red citadel above the approach to the valley, and Shahr-e-Gholghola, the ruined hilltop city over Bamyan, put the valley’s Silk Road and later history into the ground you walk across. More time in Bamyan Market afterwards. Food & culture: aush, the Afghan noodle soup.

title: The Blue Lakes of Band-e-Amir
description: A full day to Band-e-Amir National Park and its chain of blue lakes. Park access remains conditional on the season, the road and the visitor restrictions in force; if the lakes are not possible, the day becomes additional time in the Bamyan valley. We do not force the lakes in bad conditions. Back in Bamyan, the dairy market and a qurut experience: the dried yogurt at the heart of highland cooking. Food & culture: local dairy products and qurut.

title: Return to Kabul
description: The road back from Bamyan through the central highlands. This day also absorbs road, weather and other delays, so the Kabul stops are conditional: Sakhi Shrine and the view over the city from TV Hill are added only if time allows. Food & culture: bolani.

title: Kabul’s Living Culture and Historic Streets
description: A full day in Kabul’s older streets: Masjid-e Do Shamshira, the Mosque of the Two Swords by the Kabul River; Kahfroshi Bird Market in the old bazaar lanes; and the panorama from Wazir Akbar Khan Hill. A traditional Afghan box-camera portrait, associated with Mir Zaman, subject to arrangement. Completed Afghan clothing is collected today if it was arranged on Day 1. Food & culture: Qabuli palaw.

title: Farewell to Afghanistan
description: Final shopping on Chicken Street, subject to your departure time, then the airport transfer with departure assistance. Food & culture: a last cup of Afghan green tea.

title: Welcome to Springtime Kabul
description: Airport reception and hotel transfer, with sightseeing scheduled around your flight arrival time. A traditional Afghan clothing and tailoring experience (whether the clothing itself is included in the price is confirmed on your written proposal), then Babur’s Gardens in spring and the city panorama from Wazir Akbar Khan Hill. Food & culture: Afghan kabob.

title: Kabul’s Historic Heritage
description: A full Kabul heritage day linking the Kabul National Museum, Darulaman Palace, Sakhi Shrine and the view across the city from TV Tower Hill. Food & culture: Qabuli palaw.

title: Fly to Herat and Explore the Old City
description: Domestic flight from Kabul to Herat, subject to the airline schedule on the day. After arrival, Herat’s old city and bazaars, with a first introduction to the Herat Citadel above the rooftops. Food & culture: saffron tea.

title: Herat’s Architectural Treasures
description: A full day on Herat’s Timurid-era architecture: the tilework of the Herat Friday Mosque, the Herat Citadel, the Herat Minarets, and more time in the old city and bazaars. Food & culture: saffron tea.

title: Return to Kabul
description: Return flight from Herat to Kabul. Chicken Street is added only if the flight arrives in time. Food & culture: Afghan green tea.

title: Journey Through the Highlands to Bamyan
description: A full road day by private 4WD into the central highlands. The road is chosen that week for conditions; on the southern route it climbs through the Wardak Highlands. Arrival is planned for daylight, with the Buddha Niches and Bamyan Market. Food & culture: aush.

title: Discover Ancient Bamyan
description: Shahr-e-Gholghola, the ruined hilltop city above the valley; Shahr-e-Zohak, the red citadel above the approach to Bamyan; and Dragon Valley, the rock ridge tied to the valley’s dragon legend. Food & culture: mantu.

title: The Blue Lakes of Band-e-Amir
description: Band-e-Amir National Park, subject to access: the season, the road and visitor restrictions decide whether the lakes are possible. Koh-e-Baba Mountain Range scenery on the day. If the park cannot be reached, the day stays in the Bamyan area. Food & culture: Afghan green tea.

title: Return to Kabul and Cultural Farewell
description: Day 9 is a road-transfer day from Bamyan to Kabul, and the drive comes first. The Kabul activities depend on the time the road leaves: the OMAR Landmine Museum, if time and access permit; a traditional Afghan box-camera portrait with Mir Zaman, by prior arrangement; and an optional, prearranged community-support visit with a consenting host organization, run with host consent, participant privacy and safeguarding in place. A traditional Afghan farewell meal closes the day.

title: Farewell to Afghanistan
description: Breakfast, then the airport transfer with departure assistance. Food & culture: Afghan green tea.
